title: Well program approval
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6 met: a decision records actor, date, rationale and conditions; an incomplete prospect risk blocks the gate; the author cannot decide their own program; a second decision is refused against the state the program was read at; conditions are stored on the approved program where DEV-05 reads them; and a decision that is not acknowledged is retained and retried unchanged. The generic approval engine (WFL-04) is not wired, which is stated on the page and recorded below.

dataModel.decision: No well-program entity existed for a prospect (EXPLORATION_PROGRAM is field-level, with no prospect, target depth, state or conditions), and the plan's own contract names the fields (OgWellProgram { Id, ProspectId, Name, Objective, TargetDepth, DepthUnit, EstimatedCost, Currency, State, Conditions[] }). With the owning module named as LifeCycle in the feature doc, two owner tables were added - the same pattern the owner approved for WELLBORE in WEL-03: WELL_PROGRAM (PROGRAM_ID, PROSPECT_ID, FIELD_ID, PROGRAM_NAME, OBJECTIVE, TARGET_DEPTH, DEPTH_OUOM, ESTIMATED_COST, CURRENCY, STATE, AUTHOR, SUBMITTED_AT, DECIDED_BY, DECIDED_AT, RATIONALE, CONDITIONS_TEXT, ROW_VERSION) and the append-only WELL_PROGRAM_DECISION (PROGRAM_ID, DECISION_SEQ_NO, DECISION, RESULTING_STATE, RATIONALE, CONDITIONS_TEXT, DECIDED_BY, DECIDED_AT).
dataModel.verified: LIFECYCLE module setup applied in 0.2 min and the SQLite database contains both tables, with keys PROGRAM_ID and (PROGRAM_ID, DECISION_SEQ_NO).

implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/WellProgramPageView.cs (route 'wellprogram': queue with age/cost/state/risk, detail, decision panel, retry, history)
implementation.wiring: OgBootstrapper (IOgWellProgramApprovals), OgApplication.WellProgramGate, catalog 'wellprogram' (OgModuleKeys.Exploration), factory, en + ar labels
implementation.tests: test/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Tests/WellProgramApprovalTests.cs (9, no database) + WellProgramGatewayTests.cs (1 opt-in, real SQLite)

commands.schema: applied for 1 module, 0.2 min; WELL_PROGRAM and WELL_PROGRAM_DECISION created with their keys

integration.database: SQLite WELL_PROGRAM, WELL_PROGRAM_DECISION, PROSPECT and PROSPECT_RISK_ASSESSMENT
integration.queue: four programs for the field (the fifth in another field is absent), each carrying its author, age, cost ('12,000,000 USD'), state and prospect risk
integration.ac2_incomplete_risk: WP-2's prospect has SEAL_RISK null, so an approval is refused with well-program-risk-incomplete and the state stays PENDING
integration.ac3_author: the author deciding their own program is refused with well-program-author-cannot-decide and the state stays PENDING
integration.ac1_recorded: an approval by 'approver' with a rationale set STATE=APPROVED, DECIDED_BY=approver, DECIDED_AT, RATIONALE, and appended one WELL_PROGRAM_DECISION row with the same actor, state and rationale
integration.ac4_second_decision: deciding the now-approved program again (with the stale record) is refused with well-program-conflict ('already decided'), the state stays APPROVED and the decision count stays 1
integration.ac5_conditions: APPROVE_WITH_CONDITIONS with two conditions set STATE=APPROVED_WITH_CONDITIONS and stored both conditions on the program row (CONDITIONS_TEXT contains '9-5/8 liner'), and the history entry carries the same list
integration.ac6_lost_ack: a trigger made the update fail for WP-4: the decision was refused, Pending held the decision with RetainedProgramId WP-4 and nothing was written (state PENDING, 0 decisions); after the trigger was removed, RetryAsync recorded the same rationale and actor without the page resubmitting anything
integration.unknown_and_empty: an unknown program id is a failure with well-program-unknown; a field with no programs is an empty queue

gates.AC-1 Approval records actor, date, ratio: pass - DecideAsync writes DECIDED_BY, DECIDED_AT, RATIONALE and CONDITIONS_TEXT on the program and appends the same four to WELL_PROGRAM_DECISION; the SQLite test reads them back from both places through the reloaded program and its history.
gates.AC-2 Approval is refused while the prosp: pass - the program carries ProspectRiskComplete, computed from PROSPECT_RISK_ASSESSMENT with the same five-element rule the prospect board and editor use (OgProspectChance.IsComplete); Validate refuses with well-program-risk-incomplete and the SQLite test confirms the row was not touched. The unit test proves every decision type is refused, not just approval.
gates.AC-3 Author cannot approve their own pro: pass - Validate compares the program's AUTHOR with the decision's actor (case-insensitive) and refuses with well-program-author-cannot-decide; the unit test and the SQLite test both prove it, and the state is unchanged afterwards.
gates.AC-4 A second concurrent decision is ref: pass - the decision is guarded twice: the service re-reads STATE and ROW_VERSION immediately before the write and refuses with well-program-conflict if either moved, and the UPDATE itself carries STATE='PENDING' AND ROW_VERSION=<read> in its WHERE clause. The SQLite test decides an approved program a second time and sees the refusal, the unchanged state and one decision row.
gates.AC-5 Conditions appear on the resulting: pass - an approval with conditions stores the list on the program row (CONDITIONS_TEXT, one condition per line) and in the decision history; we could not test DEV-05's consumption because DEV-05 is not built, so the proof stops at 'the approved program carries its conditions in a column DEV-05 reads' - the SQLite test reads the column back.
gates.AC-6 A lost acknowledgement retains the: pass - a failed or unacknowledged write sets Pending and RetainedProgramId; RetryAsync re-reads the program and re-sends the retained decision (same actor, rationale and conditions). The SQLite test forces a real failure with a trigger, proves nothing was written, removes the trigger and retries successfully.

limits: The generic approval engine (WFL-04 / ApprovalWorkflowEngine) is not wired: delegation, escalation, quorum and role-based approvers are unavailable, and the gate records its own decision in WELL_PROGRAM/WELL_PROGRAM_DECISION instead of PROCESS_APPROVAL. The page states this in a sentence shown whatever the state, and the smoke asserts it.
WELL_PROGRAM and WELL_PROGRAM_DECISION are a new LifeCycle-owned model, not PPDM 3.9; an existing database needs the LIFECYCLE module applied again to gain them.
Submitting a program (DRAFT to PENDING) is not built: the queue reads programs that are already pending, which module seeding or a later submission screen must create.

The concurrency guard is a re-read followed by a guarded update; SQLite cannot report affected rows through this datasource, so a race between the re-read and the update is narrowed but not eliminated by a single atomic statement.
AC-5 is only half provable here: the conditions are stored for DEV-05, but DEV-05 does not exist, so nothing consumes them yet.
Evidence attachments on the program are not modelled; there is no document table link in this feature.

The retry recomputes the decision timestamp on success rather than reusing the original instant, so the retained content (actor, rationale, conditions) is identical but the recorded time is the retry's.
The page is exercised by construction (the smoke builds every catalog page and audits it) and by unit/integration tests; no automated click drives the queue or the decision panel.
